first_impression: This looks like a proper little indie game, not a jam toy: the felt-panel UI, the chunky serif title and the season map with nine named evenings sell it right away. The low-poly sheep are adorable up close (evening-5-dawn), and every evening seems to add a real twist. My worry is that the default top-down view spends a lot of the screen on empty olive grass, and the one shot that should be the scariest (the wolf in e1-wolf) is the hardest to read.
best_things: The structure: a season map from midsummer to first snow, stars, ribbons for optional challenges, unlockable charms and a daily 'Friday's Evening' slot give me clear reasons to play the next one and come back tomorrow (season-map.jpg, season-map-after-1.jpg).

Each evening card teaches exactly one new idea in plain words, lambs that follow their mothers, a ram you stare down, mist where you listen for bleats, thunder that scatters the flock, a judged trial with gates in order, so the variety looks designed rather than padded.

Some scenes are genuinely gorgeous: the snowy pass with the dark bridge and teal burn (evening-8-snow), the moonlit night watch with the flock bunched by the stream (evening-5-night), and the golden dawn with the flock round Pip (evening-5-dawn).

worst_problems.problem: The low tilted view turns the wolf moment into mush: huge see-through pine cones fill the foreground, Pip is a tiny black sliver behind a tree, and the wolf is jammed at the bottom edge half under the stamina bar. The banner says a wolf is stalking my flock but I cannot see where it is going or which sheep it wants.
worst_problems.suggestion: Pull the camera back to the normal view (or clear the trees out of the shot) when a wolf shows up, and keep the wolf, its target and Pip all in the middle of the screen.

worst_problems.problem: The default herding camera shows a lot of flat olive grass with Pip alone in the middle and the sheep off screen, marked only by little edge icons. As a still it reads as 'a dog in a field' rather than 'a dog working a flock'.
worst_problems.suggestion: Frame the dog and the nearest flock together more often, or zoom out when the flock is just off screen, so the herding relationship is always on screen.

worst_problems.problem: The first evening looks far too short and easy: the result card says every sheep home with 4:14 of daylight left, and the wolf only appeared as the job was already done. The whole 'before nightfall' hook never kicks in on the first night.
worst_problems.suggestion: Spread the first flocks further out or make the first evening shorter, so a new player actually sees the sun go down and meets a wolf with sheep still on the hill.

worst_problems.problem: From behind or head-on Pip reads as a black and white blob, more panda than collie, and at night the outlined animal in the foreground looks so wolfish that I could not tell at a glance whether it was my dog or a wolf.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give Pip a more readable shape from above and behind (ears, plumed tail out to the side) and a colour cue that is clearly 'you', like a coloured collar or ground marker, especially at night.

worst_problems.problem: In the dark menu backgrounds the sheep turn into grey and black lumps that look like boulders, and the Glenbrae Trial, billed as the whole glen watching, shows just an empty field with gate posts in the shot I saw.
worst_problems.suggestion: Light the background flocks so they read as sheep, and put the show crowd, flags or a judge's stand in view during the trial so it feels like an event.

boredom_points: Long drives across open grass with nothing in the frame but Pip and the reach ring (e1-herding): if most of the playtime looks like this, it will feel like walking more than herding.

The night watch could be a lot of standing next to a bunched flock while a dawn timer runs (evening-5-night shows a 3:45 countdown with everyone already safe); it depends on how often something actually happens.
If the early evenings are as quick as evening 1 (won with over four minutes to spare), the first few levels could feel like a tutorial with no tension.
confusions: In evening-5-night I could not tell if the white-outlined animal in front of the flock was Pip or a wolf.

The season map after evening 1 shows only Swift Paws earned, but later evening cards offer all four charms with 'wear two charms' and a 'Your best' of two stars on evenings I had not seen unlocked; I am not sure what I actually have.

The evening numbers jump around in the screenshots (the Night Watch result card says evening 6 while the trial is 5 and the mist card says 7), which is fine on the map but confusing when following the stills.
In e1-first-home the 'Pip's reach' ring is a dashed circle but the heart over the sheep at the gate and the gold ring there are not explained.
wish_list: A clear, dramatic camera for wolf attacks that keeps the wolf, the target sheep and Pip in one readable frame.
More moments where the default camera shows the valley and the sunset sky, since the setting is the selling point.
Cosmetic unlocks for Pip (collars, bandanas) or a farm that changes as the season goes on, on top of the charms.
A free-play or endless 'one more evening' mode after the season, and leaderboards for the daily evening.
Visible crowd and judges at the trial, and a replay of your trial run with the score breakdown.
one_line_review: A cosy, handsome sheepdog season with a fresh twist every evening and real reasons to come back; just let me actually see the wolves and the flock when it counts.
